To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the bioassay of hCG in pregnancy serum gives higher values than those of the fluoroimmuno‐assay and radioligand receptor assay.
the bioactivity and immunoreactivity of hCG are different in early pregnancy serum and are not correlated.

hCG levels measured in early pregnancy serum by bioassay, radioreceptorassays and fluoroimmunassay differ by a factor of 1.4‐1.7, and that the correlation between the results obtained with these methods are high.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an in‐vitro test for the detection of human chorionic gonadotrphic (hCG).
the study of the structure and function of the human chorionic gonadoptrophin (hCQ) molecule.
the study of the biological and immunological activities of hCG in maternal serum during early pregnancy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
hCG is an immunologically heterogeneous molecule, the biological potency and immunological activity of which are dependent on the molecular heterogeneity of the molecule.

hCG measured by bioassays is a mixture of different molecular forms with varying degrees of biological activity, while the hormone assayed with fluoroimmuno‐assay is a mixture of molecules with different antigenic properties.
the hCG in the serum of pregnant women is a mixture of different forms of the hormone, and that the biological and immunological activities of hCG are different in the same serum sample.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the biological activity and binding activity are more closely associated with each other than with the immunological activity of hCG in early pregnancy serum.

the bioassay is more suitable for measuring the biological activity of hCG in serum than radioreceptorassays and fluoroimmu‐noassays, and that the radioreceptorassayas are more specific for the hormone than the fluoroimmuno‐assay.
bioassay and radioligandassay are superior to fluoroimmunoasay in the determination of biological and immunological activity of hCG in pregnancy serum during first 14 weeks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the biological activity of human chorionic gonadottropin is much higher than the immunological activity in early pregnancy.
there are many different ways to measure hCG.
the biological activity of hCG in pregnancy sera can be measured using the Leydig cell bioassay and the radioreceptor assay.
